physics_findings: The exact deterministic unsteady translating-sphere impedance is retained in both models. Its s^2 term supplies fluid added mass once; the particle inertia is separately included once.

The source is a positive white-force approximation propagated through the exact causal hydrodynamic mobility. It gives 2 k_B T (6 pi eta a)|mobility|^2 instead of the equilibrium spectrum 2 k_B T Re(Z)|mobility|^2. This is a physical thermal-force closure, not a missing deterministic response term or PSD normalization error.

The independent reference solves the two decaying radial modes and integrates surface traction and the local fluctuating-stress covariance. The full symmetric strain, both off-diagonal contributions, pressure amplitude and drag sign give the correct factor: force-noise spectrum 4 k_B T eta integral(D:D*) and dissipation 2 eta integral(D:D*).

The steady branch is regular at zero frequency. The declared finite-frequency incompressible continuum regime and two-sided angular-frequency velocity spectrum are explicit; the task makes no extrapolated microscopic equipartition claim.
SI conversions, current force/velocity phase convention, positive scalar spectrum, frequency reflection and conjugate mobility conventions are consistent.

public_input_review.details: Uniform equilibrium fluid temperature, no-slip sphere, unbounded fluid, particle and fluid densities, force convention, stationary velocity readout and units uniquely define the response. Public fit is unfinished with parameter None; the separate completed shortcut uses the same forward approximation. Only public files enter the image.

calibration_and_grading.finding: DC plus complex finite-frequency response calibrates the common viscosity through the exact shared deterministic model. The DC response is strictly monotone in viscosity; sampled full-range fit checks support recovery. Parameter defaults and instrument uncertainty do not reveal the private truth.
